title: An A-module on a scheme with quasi-coherent algebra A is quasi-coherent over A exactly when it is quasi-coherent over the structure sheaf
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement is the scalar-restriction lemma for a quasi-coherent algebra A on a scheme: an A-module is quasi-coherent over the structure sheaf exactly when it is quasi-coherent over A (statement lines 2061-2070). The counted proof does both directions concretely: the first reads quasi-coherence over the structure sheaf off a local A-module presentation regarded over the smaller sheaf of rings, and the second descends to an affine chart, where the algebra and the module become an R-algebra A and an R-module M with an A-module structure, and then transfers a presentation of M over A back to a presentation of the sheaf over the tilde of A using exactness of the tilde functor (proof lines 2072-2108). It is H2: the argument is complete and self-contained and the only input is the standard local presentation of quasi-coherent modules, so no H3 claim is made.
